title: fr.linagora.twalk.inbound.message.received.v1
description: A message received from an external messaging network, decrypted by the Sensor and normalized as a CloudEvents 1.0 envelope. Produced by the Sensor after successful Megolm decryption of an m.room.message event in a Matrix portal room. Consumed by Hermes personas subscribed to the inbound.message.received.* subject on NATS JetStream. One event of this type has two shapes, selected by the sender's consent state: the full shape, and the reduced shape a 'revoked' sender's message is published in — same envelope, same relations, no content (see the 'A revoked sender's message carries no content' rule at the end of this schema, and ADR 0012).

specversion.description: CloudEvents specification version. Fixed to 1.0 for all Twalk v1 events.

id.description: Deterministic identifier computed as sha256(matrix_event_id + ':' + matrix_room_id). Ensures idempotent replay: the same underlying Matrix event always produces the same CloudEvents id, so consumers can deduplicate safely across bus resynchronizations.

source.description: URI identifying the Matrix room where the event originated. Format: matrix://<homeserver>/<room_id>. The homeserver is the Synapse instance operated by Twalk; the room_id is the portal room maintained by the Mautrix bridge.

type.description: CloudEvents type. Reverse-DNS convention with an explicit version suffix. Any breaking change to this schema requires incrementing the suffix (v2, v3, ...) rather than mutating v1.

time.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the Sensor produced the event, not the original network timestamp. The original network timestamp is preserved in data.network_timestamp when available.

subject.description: Matrix user ID of the observed sender, as materialized by the bridge (e.g. @whatsapp_33612345678:example.com). Used for routing and for consent evaluation. Always a person the bridge stands in for — a ghost, or a native Matrix account (ADR 0009) — and never the deployment owner (ADR 0021) nor a bridge's own bot, the appservice service identity named by its sender_localpart (ADR 0026): neither is a contact, neither has a consent state, and nothing is published about a bridge bot on any type.

datacontenttype.description: Fixed to application/json for all Twalk v1 events. Binary payloads (images, files) are referenced by URL in data.attachments and stored separately in Matrix media storage.

dataschema.description: Optional URI pointing back to this JSON Schema. Recommended for third-party consumers that validate events dynamically.

traceparent.description: Optional W3C Trace Context traceparent header. Enables distributed tracing across Sensor, NATS, Hermes and downstream services without mandating a specific tracing backend.

network.description: Twalk extension. Identifies the external network the message originated from, as the user experiences it; transport bridges (e.g. mautrix-gmessages) are never network values. The value matrix is native Matrix traffic: a room with no m.bridge state event and no ghost-prefixed sender, reached through the user's own Matrix account instead of through a bridge (see ADR 0009). Enables server-side filtering on NATS without deserializing the data payload.

connection.description: Twalk extension (ADR 0033). The **connection** this event belongs to: the one configured account — a bridge, a mailbox, a calendar — the deployment observed it on or acts through, by the opaque stable id the deployment gave it (`whatsapp`, `mail-linagora`). `network` says what kind of thing that is; this says which one. Two facts, two fields: a deployment with two bridges of one network has two connections, and a consent decision is scoped to a connection. On a deployment with one connection per network the id is the network's name, which is what every existing decision was migrated onto. The Companion Gateway keeps the registry (`GET /api/connections`); a producer never derives an id, it is handed one.

consent.description: Twalk extension. Current consent state of the sender's data-processing agreement, as tracked by the Companion Gateway, the single writer of consent state. Personas MUST refuse to process events where consent is not 'granted', unless they are explicitly authorized to handle consent-management workflows. The value also selects which shape of this event type the producer publishes: 'revoked' means the reduced shape, carrying no content at all (ADR 0012); 'granted' and 'pending' mean the full shape — a pending sender's message is labelled, never reduced.

body.description: The message content in its canonical text form. For messages with rich formatting, the plain-text fallback. Required unless the sender's consent is 'revoked', in which case a producer MUST omit it: the field is what carries the message, and a revoked contact's content is not collected (ADR 0012). For a media message the canonical text form is the caption, or the filename when there is none, so omitting the body is also what keeps a revoked sender's filenames off the bus.

format.description: Content type of the body field. text/plain is the default and safest; text/html is only used when the source network provided HTML-formatted content.

matrix_event_id.description: The Matrix event ID of the message being replied to.

excerpt.description: A short excerpt of the replied-to message for context, so consumers do not need to look it up to reason about the reply. Required unless the sender's consent is 'revoked', in which case a producer MUST omit it: an excerpt is message content, quoted rather than sent, and the relation alone (matrix_event_id) is what the reduced event keeps.

reply_to.description: If the message is a reply to a previous one, structured reference to the parent. Null otherwise.

mxc_uri.description: Matrix content URI, resolvable via the homeserver media API. Required unless the sender's consent is 'revoked', in which case a producer MUST omit it, together with encryption and caption: a reference to the bytes, and the key that opens them, is the content — what a reduced attachment keeps is its shape (kind, mime_type, size_bytes, dimensions, duration_ms), which describes the message without carrying it (ADR 0012).

mime_type.description: IANA media type of the attachment.

caption.description: Optional caption provided with the attachment. Text the sender wrote, so it is content: never published when the sender's consent is 'revoked'.

dimensions.description: Pixel dimensions for image and video attachments.

duration_ms.description: Duration in milliseconds for audio and video attachments.

kty.description: JSON Web Key type. Always oct (a symmetric octet sequence) for Matrix attachment encryption.

key_ops.description: Permitted key operations. Must contain at least encrypt and decrypt, per the Matrix EncryptedFile definition. Order is not significant, and the specification permits further operations, so consumers test for membership rather than comparing the whole array.

alg.description: Key algorithm. Always A256CTR (AES-256 in counter mode) for version v2 attachment encryption.

k.description: The 256-bit AES key, URL-safe unpadded base64. This is decryption material for the user's own media: consumers MUST keep it inside the user's infrastructure and MUST NOT log it.

ext.description: JSON Web Key extractability flag. Always true, so the key can be imported by a consumer's crypto implementation.

key.description: The AES key as a JSON Web Key, exactly as carried by the Matrix event.

iv.description: The 128-bit unique counter block used by AES-CTR, standard-alphabet unpadded base64 (22 characters). Note the alphabet differs from key.k, which the Matrix specification encodes URL-safe.

sha256.description: SHA-256 digest of the ciphertext, standard-alphabet unpadded base64 (43 characters). Consumers MUST verify it before decrypting: it is what stops the homeserver from substituting the media bytes.

hashes.description: Digests of the ciphertext, keyed by algorithm. The Matrix specification types this as an open map and only recommends sha256; the contract carries sha256 and nothing else, so every consumer has exactly one digest to verify and one algorithm to implement.

v.description: Version of the attachment encryption scheme. v2 is the only version the Matrix specification defines; material from the pre-specification v1 scheme is not usable by consumers and is not published.

encryption.description: Optional decryption material for an attachment whose ciphertext is what mxc_uri resolves to. Mirrors the Matrix EncryptedFile object (key, iv, hashes, v) defined under 'Sending encrypted attachments' in the client-server specification, minus its url field, which mxc_uri already carries, and minus a mimetype, which the specification keeps in info and the contract keeps in mime_type. Present when the media itself is encrypted, which is the normal case in an end-to-end encrypted room and therefore in every bridge portal room; absent for media served in the clear. Producers re-serialize the values in the canonical encodings below rather than copying the sender's JSON through, so consumers handle exactly one encoding; a producer that cannot fill this object completely (an unsupported protocol version, or no sha256 digest) publishes the attachment without it rather than publishing unusable material. Either way the message is delivered and never silently dropped, but without this object a consumer can fetch the bytes and not read them. Never published when the sender's consent is 'revoked': decryption material is what turns a reference into content, so it goes where mxc_uri goes.

attachments.description: Ordered list of attachments carried by the message. Only references and decryption material ever transit the bus; the bytes stay in Matrix media storage.

display_name.description: Human-readable display name of the sender, as known to the recipient.

network_identifier.description: Optional native network identifier (e.g. phone number for WhatsApp, username for Telegram). Only populated when consent state allows it.

avatar_mxc_uri.description: Optional Matrix content URI for the contact's avatar.

contact.description: Structured information about the sender, resolved by Sensor from the Matrix membership state and bridge metadata.

network_timestamp.description: Optional RFC 3339 timestamp of the original event as reported by the source network, when the bridge provides it. Distinct from the top-level 'time' attribute, which is the Sensor's own timestamp.

thread_root.description: Optional Matrix event ID of the thread root, if the message is part of a Matrix thread.

allOf.title: A revoked sender's message carries no content
allOf.description: The two shapes of this event type, made checkable so a third-party producer reduces exactly like the Sensor (ADR 0012). The branch reads the envelope's own 'consent' extension — the top-level attribute, not a field of 'data' — so a validator decides from the event alone, with no outside lookup. When it is 'revoked', every field that carries the message is forbidden: data.body, data.reply_to.excerpt, and each attachment's mxc_uri, encryption and caption. What stays is the evidence that a message arrived — the deterministic id, the network, both timestamps, the room and sender references, the reply and thread relations, the contact's display name — plus each attachment's shape. Otherwise ('granted' or 'pending') the full shape applies and those fields are required as they were in v1 before this rule: a pending sender's message is labelled, never reduced.
